questions.question: What are the five primitives of the OpenAI Agents SDK?
options: Model, Prompt, Tool, Memory, Trace
Agent, Handoff, Guardrail, Session, Tracing
Actor, Message, Router, Worker, Monitor
Chain, Node, Edge, State, Checkpoint
questions.explanation: The OpenAI Agents SDK has five primitives: Agent (LLM + instructions + tools + handoffs), Handoff (delegation to another agent), Guardrail (input/output/tool validation), Session (automatic conversation history), and Tracing (built-in spans).

questions.question: How does the OpenAI Agents SDK represent handoffs to the model?
options: As a special API call the runtime intercepts
As a function tool named 'transfer_to_<agent_name>' in the model's tool list
As a system prompt instruction to switch agents
As a metadata field in the message header
questions.explanation: Handoffs are represented to the model as a function tool named transfer_to_<agent_name>. When the model calls this tool, the runtime copies conversation context and initializes the target agent to continue the run.

questions.question: What is the difference between parallel and blocking guardrail modes?
options: Parallel guardrails run before the main LLM; blocking guardrails run after
Parallel: guardrail LLM runs alongside the main LLM (lower latency, wastes tokens on trip); Blocking: guardrail runs first (no token waste but higher latency on trip)
Parallel guardrails check multiple conditions; blocking guardrails check one condition
Parallel guardrails are async; blocking guardrails are synchronous
questions.explanation: Parallel mode (default): the guardrail LLM runs alongside the main LLM. Lower tail latency, but if the guardrail trips, the main LLM's tokens are wasted. Blocking mode: guardrail runs first. If it trips, no tokens wasted, but latency is higher.

questions.question: What exception does a guardrail raise when it trips?
options: GuardrailViolation
InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered or OutputGuardrailTripwireTriggered
AgentPolicyError
SafetyCheckFailed
questions.explanation: When a guardrail detects a policy violation, it raises InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered (for input guardrails) or OutputGuardrailTripwireTriggered (for output guardrails). The agent can catch these and handle appropriately.

questions.question: What is the 'handoff drift' failure mode and how is it mitigated?
options: Handoffs take too long; mitigate by running them asynchronously
Agent A hands off to Agent B which hands back to Agent A indefinitely; mitigate by adding a hop counter
Handoffs lose context; mitigate by copying all messages
The model forgets what was being worked on after a handoff; mitigate with system prompt reminders
questions.explanation: Handoff drift occurs when agents bounce between each other (A -> B -> A -> B) without converging. Add a hop counter that refuses handoffs after N transfers to prevent infinite bouncing.

questions.question: What does the OpenAI Agents SDK's tracing behavior by default?
options: Tracing is disabled by default to protect privacy
Tracing is on by default: every LLM generation, tool call, handoff, and guardrail emits a span
Only errors are traced by default
Tracing must be explicitly configured per agent
questions.explanation: The OpenAI Agents SDK has tracing on by default. Every LLM generation, tool call, handoff, and guardrail emits a span. Use OPENAI_AGENTS_DISABLE_TRACING=1 to opt out, or add_trace_processor() to fan spans to additional backends.
